notes.executionRules: The 'Shared execution rules' and the 'Session-264 dispatch' section in the index impl-plans/active/search-engine-adapter.md are binding. All workers run on branch main in one working directory. Workers run no git write commands and create no worktrees or branches. Before each edit, fresh-read the file and record its shasum -a 256, and record the post-edit hash in the worker's own plan Progress Log. Before the first edit, copy the plan to tmp/search-engine-adapter/<P#>/plan-snapshot.md as an immutable intent snapshot. Edit only your own writePaths. sharedPaths are read-only unless a sharedPathNotes entry grants a specific edit. Never touch .riela/, the index (except P11 and P21), other plans' files or lockfiles. Run no broad formatters.
notes.evidenceLayout: Evidence lives under the untracked, gitignored evidenceRoot tmp/search-engine-adapter, with one subdirectory per plan short id (P3, P7, P8, P9, P11, P12..P21). A re-run writes to attempt-<n>/ and keeps earlier logs. Run mkdir -p first, because tee does not create directories.
notes.gateEvidence: A behavioral verification record has a command matching swift test, bun test, vitest run, or mise run <name containing test>; exitCode 0; and every count key (testsRun/testsPassed/testCount) > 0, with the full log path and final exit status. Record XCTest 'Executed N tests, 0 failures' counts. A filtered run's swift-testing '0 tests' line is not a count record. The env-gated skip of ElasticsearchLiveTests is a non-behavioral note, never evidence. P9, P11, P20 and P21 record cd web && mise exec -- bun test src and cd web && mise exec -- bunx vitest run separately; mise run web:check and tauri:check are supporting records without counts. For each swift test --filter record, record only the count of the framework that actually ran the matched tests: XCTest Executed N tests, or swift-testing Test run with N tests passed. Never record a 0 count from the other framework. Tests/KaibaClientTests, CommandCLITests, SearchEngineContractTests and KaibaSearchEngineConfigurationDecodingTests are swift-testing. New test files use XCTest, except in KaibaClientTests.
notes.shell: Verification commands use the bash-only ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, so they are wrapped in bash -c. A blank exit= is not evidence. Swift tests need PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$PWD/.build/anydoc-native/host/pkgconfig. Run mise run build once first. bun is reachable only through mise exec or mise run.
notes.peerBreaks: Concurrent workers in a wave share one .build. A compile failure in a file outside your writePaths that belongs to another in-flight plan is not yours to edit. Retry up to 3 times, about 2 minutes apart. After that, record 'blocked by peer <planId>', never 'passed'. P11 (base) or P21 (delta) re-runs it.
notes.fileOwnership: One owner per wave for each hot file. SearchEngine.swift: P12 (wave 1). NoteService.swift: P12 (wave 1), then P14 (wave 2). Elasticsearch*.swift and SearchEngineFactory.swift: P3 (wave 1, evidence only), then P13 (wave 2). NoteService+SearchEngine.swift: P15 (wave 2). CommandSearchEngine.swift: P7 (wave 1), then P17 (wave 3). KaibaServerRuntime.swift: P8 (wave 1), then P19 (wave 4). GraphQL schema, registries and executor: P18 (wave 4). web files: P9 (wave 1, evidence only), then P20 (wave 2). ElasticsearchLiveTests.swift: P13 (wave 2, index name), then P21 (wave 6). notes.commitPolicy: AGENTS.md governs commits: no emojis, no machine-local absolute paths, no secrets, and no AI attribution in commit messages. .riela/ stays untracked and is never committed; tmp/ is gitignored. Workers do not commit. P11 and P21 do not commit, push or archive plans; workflow finalization owns that.
notes.dockerPolicy: The operator keeps the compose Elasticsearch running (mise run search:up). P3, P11, P13 and P21 run KAIBA_ELASTICSEARCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9200 mise run search:test-live. Check mise run search:status first. If Docker is unavailable, record 'blocked: docker unavailable' with the exact error, never passed. Only a plan that started the cluster stops it.
notes.secretPolicy: No test secret literal may appear in any committed file other than test sources, and none may appear in evidence logs. Settings secrets are write-only, stored as {authMode, target, secret} under auth.search-engine.secret, and reused only when both authMode and the normalized target are unchanged.
notes.artifactPolicy: Every plan declares artifactRoots: [] because no plan installs tools or downloads into a declared path. Build and tool outputs land outside every writePaths/sharedPaths entry: .build/, web/node_modules, web/dist, web/src-tauri/target, the evidence root tmp/search-engine-adapter, and the Docker image and volume. If a generated or binary file under a declared path becomes necessary, stop and record it in the Progress Log so the plan can be amended.

reviewContext.issueReference: No GitHub issue. Inline workflowInput 'Search engine adapter: finish base feature (P3/P9 evidence, P7, P8, P11) and add ontology-aware search, hybrid related notes, and engine selection/connection settings' (workflowExecutionId opus-luna-design-and-implement-review-loop-session-264; intake comm-003768; design accepted in comm-003772 after the DR-D5-SECRET-RETARGET fix).
reviewContext.userProblem: Finish the optional Elasticsearch adapter. Also make similar-note and ontology-aware search run deterministically on the engine, with tag hierarchy, classes and links and no LLM, and let administrators select the engine and edit its connection in settings, with write-only secrets, test connection and hot-swap.
requiredOutcomes: Base: P3 and P9 gate-compatible evidence; P7 CLI; P8 server sync loop; P11 base integration.

D1: engine documents carry direct and ancestor tag ids and names, classes, provenance and links. Every ontology write enqueues through the outbox, including the subtree on class change and reparent. Index -v2 with an identity that includes the normalized base URL.
D2: hierarchical tag and class filters on indexed ancestor ids, deterministic ontology expansion with boosts 4.0/2.0, and opt-in facets, across protocol, GraphQL, KaibaClient and SearchView.

D3: a hybrid relatedNotes query (linked 5.0, shared tag 3.0, shared person/event +2.0, near tag 1.5, MLT text). Reasons are confirmed against the store and shown in RelatedNotesSection. The source is excluded, and the SE4 re-check applies.
D4: the agent search_notes tool uses the engine when attached and include_linked is false, with FTS fallback on SearchEngineError. User-facing engine search has no AI types.

D5: config-locked precedence; admin-gated store settings under auth.search-engine.*; a write-only secret bound to authMode and target; a sanitized test connection with no network call on a retarget; hot-swap through the shared SearchEngineSlot and the runtime controller; a disable path; a web settings section.
nonGoals: A tag rename, merge or delete API; engine routing for AIAgenticSearch and NoteSearchPopup; env-var credentials in store settings; non-loopback plain http; automatic deletion of the -v1 index.
Changing searchNotes, NoteSearch ranking or lexical fusion.
constraints: No behavior change when no engine is selected, apart from the always-installed no-op kick observer and the settings read.
Never fail writes because of the engine; no engine call inside a store transaction.
Access is enforced in the engine filter and by the store re-check.
Secrets never appear in views, errors, logs, GraphQL responses, docs or commits.
Swift files under 1000 lines; swiftlint; web:check and tauri:check pass; the server-credential tests are unchanged.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Shared SearchEngineSlot reference: scoped NoteService copies see a hot-swapped adapter.
Settings keys under the existing reserved auth. prefix, so the ungated generic appSetting surface cannot reach them.
The secret is bound to the normalized target, so a stored credential cannot be redirected to another host (review finding DR-D5-SECRET-RETARGET).
Expansion and related-signal resolution happen in store SQL and Swift; the engine evaluates them as named, boosted clauses that produce machine-readable reasons.
intentionalTradeoffs: Engine search stays a separate GraphQL field (engineSearchNotes); engine scores never feed the FTS lexical fusion (user-qa 'Decisions taken without a user answer').

Ontology expansion is deterministic store-side tag-name matching capped at 10 tags (CJK substring, Latin whole-word) with fixed boosts, instead of semantic or LLM expansion (user-qa 'Ontology expansion').
Related-note and expansion boosts are fixed adapter constants, not per-store settings (user-qa open question).
Facets are engine aggregations over the engine-filtered set, computed only on request; counts may include notes the store re-check drops and are shown as refinement hints only (user-qa 'Facets').
A config-file searchEngine section locks the settings (managedBy config, read-only UI, settings-managed-by-config error) rather than merging with store settings (user-qa 'Config precedence').
The secret is write-only with no partial mask and must be re-entered whenever the URL or auth mode changes (user-qa 'Secret binding to target').
The index moves to -v2 and the identity includes the normalized base URL, costing a one-time backfill; the -v1 index is left for the operator to delete (design 'Delta rollout').
verifyTLS=false is offered as requested but only for https on platforms with the Security framework, with a UI warning (accepted residual DR-LOW-VERIFYTLS-SAME-TARGET).
supportedEdgeCases: No engine selected and no config section: behavior identical to FTS-only, engine UI hidden through the capability flag.
Engine outage or SearchEngineError: note writes still succeed through the durable outbox; the agent search_notes tool falls back to FTS.
Tag reparent or tag class change: every note under the affected subtree is enqueued and reindexed.
Tag filter on an ancestor tag matches notes tagged only with a descendant (indexed ancestor ids).
Query term matching a tag name matches tagged notes even when the body lacks the term, ranked by the expansion boosts.
relatedNotes excludes the source note, applies the SE4 store re-check, and confirms shared-tag reasons against the store.
Settings update or test connection that changes the URL host or auth mode without a new secret is rejected with searchEngine.secret and makes no network call.
authMode none deletes the stored secret; appSetting/setAppSetting refuse the auth.search-engine.* keys.
Test connection errors from a transport that echoes the secret are sanitized.

Hot-swap: a reload is seen by scoped NoteService copies; an index identity change triggers backfill; disabling stops the sync loop and returns notConfigured; concurrent reloads converge; an invalid stored setting at startup is not fatal.
Non-administrators get the existing not-found-shaped error and do not see the web settings section.
Existing config-file deployments become managedBy config and backfill into -v2 on first start after upgrade.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Tag rename, merge or delete flows (no API exists; a future rename must call the D1 subtree enqueue).
Engine retrieval for AIAgenticSearch grounding and the NoteSearchPopup link picker (stay on FTS).
Environment-variable credentials in store settings (config file only).
Automatic deletion of the old -v1 index and a search-engine detach command.
Facet counts that exactly match the store re-checked result set.
Alternative analyzers such as kuromoji; per-store boost tuning.
tauri:check off macOS and live Elasticsearch tests without the operator's compose cluster (recorded as blocked with the exact error, never passed).
residualRisksFromDesignReview: DR-LOW-VERIFYTLS-SAME-TARGET (low): an administrator can disable TLS verification for the same target and reuse the stored secret. This is limited to https, warned in the UI, and recorded in user-qa.
Facet counts can include notes the store re-check drops (a documented bound).
verifyTLS=false requires the Security framework; elsewhere validation rejects it.
